WHAT THE NUMBERS MEAN: about 1% of observation-level camera records are the same device as another source's record under rules whose STRICT holdout precision cleared the 0.98 floor with >= 50 holdout pairs (tier 1g 70/70, tier 3g 69/70 on the frozen agent-verified holdout). Most records have no cross-source counterpart; every uncertain candidate (proximity only, co-located devices, soft conflicts, refused unions) is proposed for review and NOT counted. Of the multi-record sites, 273 span two or more independent lineages and 2054 are republished copies within one lineage (not independent corroboration). Value-resolved coordinates (230,330) remain a separate, non-dedup figure.

The camera-site eval is PROVISIONAL: the holdout is agent-verified (not field-verified), the blind LLM adjudicator's kappa (0.669) missed the 0.70 bar so it is a suggester only, and tier 3g scores 0.800 under the LLM's labels (it reads sub-metre offsets between republished copies as proximity only) — the first-principles half of D-R6.1-EVAL stays OPEN.
camera_site_notes: gold history: rules v1 measured tier 1g 0.882 (30/34) and 3g 0.929 (39/42) on the camera-1 holdout (both demoted — nothing would have auto-written); that holdout was then inspected while diagnosing, retired to training, and rules v2 were measured on a fresh 180-pair holdout (camera-2). The later review fixes changed no rule the holdout was drawn for except distance ties (a code-review finding, not a holdout inspection); the gate re-measured the same frozen holdout at run time with an unchanged result for the auto-write tiers.
